variables.title: STEADI track screening population
variables.description: Community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older seen in ambulatory care. Inpatient, hospice and long-term-care settings are outside this track. This is the track target population, not a claim that every research participant met the three-question screening rule.

variables.title: Exercise fall-rate analysis population
variables.description: Community-dwelling older adults in the 29 exercise trials contributing to the fall-rate analysis (14,475 participants). The broader exercise evidence base included participants at average and increased fall risk; membership was not defined by this track's three-question result.

variables.title: Multifactorial fall-rate analysis population
variables.description: Community-dwelling older adults in the 20 multifactorial-intervention trials contributing to the fall-rate analysis (22,115 participants). Risk definitions and intervention protocols varied; membership was not defined by this track's three-question result.

variables.title: Exercise intervention exposure
variables.description: Exercise interventions studied for fall prevention. Across the evidence body, most included gait, balance and functional training, often with strength or resistance training. This variable describes the research exposure and prescribes no particular regimen.

variables.title: Multifactorial intervention exposure
variables.description: Assessment of modifiable fall-risk factors followed by individualized interventions. Components and implementation varied, and some trials also provided components to all participants. This describes the USPSTF evidence grouping; it is not identical to every other review's multifactorial category.

variables.title: Comparator arms of the contributing trials
variables.description: The control/comparison arms used in the contributing randomized trials for each cited pooled estimate. The supplied recommendation and abstract do not establish a single uniform control regimen; this variable does not assert usual care, placebo or no treatment for every trial.

variables.title: Rate of incident falls
variables.description: Rate of incident falls, including repeat events, at each trial's longest reported follow-up within the stated analysis range. This is distinct from the proportion of people experiencing at least one fall and from injurious falls or fractures.

evidence.title: Exercise and rate of incident falls
evidence.finding: Exercise versus contributing trial comparator arms: incidence rate ratio 0.85 (95% CI 0.75 to 0.96), 29 trials, 14,475 participants, longest follow-up 6 to 24 months. Heterogeneity I-squared = 82.7% (supplied AHRQ abstract). This estimate applies to incident fall rate, not the number of people who fall.
evidence.recommendation: The USPSTF recommends exercise interventions for community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older at increased fall risk.
evidence.netBenefit: USPSTF assessed moderate certainty of a moderate net benefit for its recommendation. This is not a certainty rating assigned by this implementation to the individual pooled estimate.
evidence.harms: About half of exercise trials reported harms. Minor musculoskeletal symptoms were most common; serious harms were rare, with exercise-associated wrist and hip fractures reported in separate trials. Sparse reporting limits certainty about harms.
evidence.limitations: Interventions, baseline risks and follow-up varied. The evidence does not select one best exercise regimen. Lack of statistically significant fracture or mortality reductions does not establish no effect.

evidence.title: Multifactorial intervention and rate of incident falls
evidence.finding: Multifactorial intervention versus contributing trial comparator arms: incidence rate ratio 0.84 (95% CI 0.74 to 0.95), 20 trials, 22,115 participants, longest follow-up 6 to 28 months. Heterogeneity I-squared = 85.0% (supplied AHRQ abstract). This estimate applies to incident fall rate, not the number of people who fall.
evidence.recommendation: The USPSTF recommends individualizing whether to offer multifactorial interventions to community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older at increased fall risk, considering prior falls, comorbidities and patient preferences.
evidence.netBenefit: USPSTF assessed moderate certainty of a small net benefit for its recommendation. Routine provision to everyone is not the recommended decision.
evidence.harms: Harms were sparsely reported; five trials with 4,199 participants reported generally rare, minor effects, often associated with exercise components.
evidence.limitations: Trial components, baseline risks, implementation and adherence varied. Pooled results did not establish statistically significant reductions in people falling, injurious falls, fractures or mortality; this is not proof of no effect.
